title: Tactile press dent and damped elastic shockwave pad
blurb: One ElementGL WebGL 2 canvas draws a live 3x2 HTML control pad that dents under pointerdown with rim shading and launches damped concentric shockwaves across neighbouring tiles on release.
question: Can one ElementGL WebGL 2 canvas dent a live 3×2 HTML control pad under pointerdown with normal-mapped rim lighting and send damped concentric elastic shockwaves across neighbouring tiles on release while keeping every button, switch and input clickable?
result: Measured in HeadlessChrome/160.0.0.0 (2026-11-27): all 6 live checks pass at 412 px (DPR 2.625, 945x877 canvas, 0.829 MP, 6.63 MB initial, 15.36 MB peak, 0 errors) and 960 px desktop (DPR 2). A held press darkens dent centre luminance from 212 to 136 while lifting the rim lip to 241 and pulling pixels inward, release waves drive up to 4 concurrent rings across neighbouring tiles (neighbour diff 334 at 280 ms, 0 at rest), and updateElementGeometry() keeps all buttons, switches and the pad label input clickable and focusable. Chrome 159 on Android and npm run check:jank stay not verified.
